stem: A games club has 40 members. Of these members, 22 play chess, 15 play checkers and 6 play both chess and checkers. If a member of the club is selected at random, what is the probability that the member plays chess or checkers (or both)?
solution: Adding 22 and 15 counts the 6 members who play both games twice.
Members who play at least one game: \(22 + 15 - 6 = 31\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This adds 22 and 15 without subtracting the 6 members who play both, so those members are counted twice.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the probability that the member plays NEITHER game: \(40 - 31 = 9\).
explanation.C: Correct. \(22 + 15 - 6 = 31\) members play at least one of the games, so the probability is \(\frac{31}{40}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{6}{40}\), the probability that the member plays BOTH games.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
p = Rational(22 + 15 - 6, 40)
assert p == Rational(31, 40)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
